A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OVOD-Agent and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and four-page appendices. All 14 pages of each version support comparison, including the image-based case study and evaluation prompts.

before.justification: v1 reports original COCO/LVIS detection experiments, exploration-strategy evaluations, component ablations, and qualitative case studies in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original detection experiments and ablations, revises trajectory-evaluation results, and reports additional detector comparisons.

M1.justification: The seven visual operators, weak Markov formulation, UCB exploration, dual-head reward model, training objective, and inference rules remain unchanged, including Algorithms 1–2. Relabeling reward-model training from self-supervised to weakly supervised does not change the already documented ground-truth-seeded procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate open-vocabulary detection on COCO and LVIS, with the same trajectory-assessment tasks and qualitative examples. The additional detector configurations do not introduce new datasets, populations, or task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 2 removes DetCLIPv3 and adds GroundingDINO 1.5 and DINO-X Pro, substantially revising the main cross-detector comparisons. Appendix Table 6 adds LLMDet alongside the retained GroundingDINO, RALF, CoT-PL, and DVDet comparisons. CoT-PL's changed description does not constitute another new comparator.

E3.justification: Figure 5 and Section 6.4 change GPT-5 evaluation from explicitly named sampling strategies to anonymized identifiers, introducing a concrete blinding control. Table 2 also uses revised detector configurations. Dataset splits, detection metrics, exploration stopping criteria, and the four trajectory-scoring criteria remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing UCB exploration analysis now includes blind AI assessments, and the Visual-CoT action ablation has a revised result. Table 4's renamed KL-regularization rows represent the existing comparison, not a new ablation. The failure examples and detailed appendix case study remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains the same ± reporting practice, and Table 4 retains its RM-loss standard-deviation metric. Neither version supplies additional repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Changed AI means do not change uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces the DetCLIPv3 results with new GroundingDINO 1.5 and DINO-X Pro results, including LVIS-val baseline/agent AP_r pairs of 42.7/44.1 and 48.0/49.2. Table 6 adds LLMDet results, including 40.8 AP_r and 35 ms average latency. Under the revised blind protocol, Table 3 changes Random's AI score from 2.8 to 3.0 and Greedy-Q's from 3.2 to 3.3. Table 5 revises full-action AP_r from 38.1 to 37.7. Retained GroundingDINO and YOLO-World main results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–15, the short-term Markov assumption, transition priors, and mathematical objectives remain unchanged. Adding 'Decision' to the weak-Markov subsection terminology does not revise the formulation. No new theorem, proof, or derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace the self-supervised reward-model claim with weakly supervised training, aligning the claim with the existing ground-truth-based reward initialization. The central claims of lightweight, LLM-free visual reasoning and improvements across detector backbones remain.

C2.justification: Section 6.3 now distinguishes online RALF reasoning from offline LLM use by CoT-PL, DVDet, and LLMDet, shifting criticism toward preprocessing and training costs. It replaces the explanation of roughly 2.2 reasoning steps with a claimed 2.2× inference speedup unsupported by a corresponding comparison. The two failure-mode limitations are condensed without substantive changes.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 identifies API access for the newly evaluated detectors, and Figure 5 supplies the revised anonymized evaluation template. Table 6 removes the shared GroundingDINO-B specification and replaces numerical LLM-call counts with usage categories. Operator pseudocode, software-toolkit disclosures, and existing method settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to LLMDet, GroundingDINO 1.5, and DINO-X, and revises appendix positioning around online versus offline LLM dependence. The main related-work narrative is retained. Detic reference deduplication and DetCLIP publication-metadata updates are editorial rather than changes in cited research.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites of the results discussion, limitations, and appendix comparison/scoring sections, plus supervision-terminology and heading changes. The overall section sequence and most methodological prose remain intact. The unsupported promise of additional cross-detector appendix ablations is removed.

P2.justification: Figure 5 is redrawn for anonymous scoring. Tables 2 and 6 change their row sets, Table 6 replaces the LLM Calls column with LLM Usage, and Tables 3–4 revise captions or labels. Figure 2 moves from page 3 to page 4; the other figure artwork remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: Blind trajectory scoring and the corrected supervision claim improve methodological clarity, while added detector comparisons broaden the evidence. However, Table 6 loses its explicit common-backbone assurance, and Section 6.3 introduces an unsupported 2.2× speedup claim and groups CoT-PL with 30–35 ms methods despite its retained 1.2-second table entry. These new inconsistencies weaken the efficiency argument and leave the comparability of the expanded evidence unclear, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
